hero.sub: I manage 500+ WordPress & Shopify sites, and I build the dashboards, plugins, and tooling needed to run them at scale. Google Cloud, AWS, and AI integrations when the project calls for it.

tools.name: WP Hub
tools.tagline: One dashboard for a 500-site WordPress fleet.
tools.description: Aggregates every site through the WP REST API: plugin and theme update status, server health, last-login activity, and a quick-jump link into any admin panel. Built because per-site maintenance stopped scaling.

tools.name: Server Checker
tools.tagline: Scheduled uptime, SSL, and response-code monitoring.
tools.description: Pings the whole fleet on a schedule and checks SSL validity, response codes, and server health, then alerts by email or webhook on failure. Replaced per-site third-party monitoring that would have cost more than the sites earn.

tools.name: Git-backed CMS
tools.tagline: The admin panel that edits this site. No backend.
tools.description: A single dependency-free HTML file that reads and writes content.json straight through the GitHub Contents API. Image uploads become commits, saving triggers the Actions build, and there is no server, database, or hosting bill anywhere in the loop.
tools.demoNote: Runs at /admin and needs a GitHub token, so no open demo.

projects.title: WP Hub
projects.tagline: Internal dashboard for managing 500+ WordPress sites.
projects.summary: A custom-built multi-site management hub to monitor, update, and maintain a large fleet of WordPress sites from a single interface, replacing manual per-site work with centralised ops.

sections.heading: the problem
sections.body: Managing 500+ WordPress sites manually was unsustainable. Each site needed updates, monitoring, and quick-access admin. Doing this one-by-one was hours of overhead daily.

sections.heading: how it works
sections.body: A centralised dashboard aggregates all sites via the WP REST API. One login shows plugin and theme update status, server health, and last-login activity, with quick-jump links into any admin panel.

sections.heading: where it stands
sections.body: Multi-site maintenance overhead is down roughly 80%. Updates that used to take half a day now run in minutes from a single screen, and the tool is still in daily use.

projects.title: Early Bird College
projects.tagline: Custom admissions dashboard with a database-backed AI chat.
projects.summary: A fully custom WordPress-powered dashboard for Early Bird College, handling student applications, tracking progress, and managing enrolments through a bespoke plugin and UI, plus an AI chat that answers prospective students from the live database.

sections.heading: the brief
sections.body: The client needed one place to manage student enrolments and track application progress. Existing plugins couldn't handle their specific workflow, so the admissions process was still running on spreadsheets.

sections.heading: two systems, one surface
sections.body: WordPress handles the student-facing frontend: data collection forms, user accounts, and content. Django runs the backend, covering payment processing, enrolment logic, and the iframe management layer that ties both systems together.

sections.heading: the AI chat
sections.body: Prospective students kept asking the same questions about colleges, courses, and enrolment steps, and every one landed on staff. I built the chat from scratch and wired it into Django so it queries the live database instead of guessing, meaning it answers from real records and says so when there is no match. Repeat enquiries reaching staff dropped noticeably.

sections.heading: result
sections.body: A manual spreadsheet-based process became a live dashboard, saving staff hours per week and cutting enrolment errors.

projects.title: ITBS Business Tracking
projects.tagline: Custom business tracking dashboard for Identity Theft Business Solutions.
projects.summary: A bespoke business tracking dashboard built into the client's Duda site, letting them manage and monitor business identity theft cases, client records, and service statuses in one place.

sections.heading: the constraint
sections.body: The client needed a proprietary tracking system for business identity theft cases. No off-the-shelf CRM fit their service model, and the public site was locked to Duda.

sections.heading: decoupled by design
sections.body: The public-facing site stays on Duda. The tracking dashboard is a separate app hosted on GitHub Pages, deployed via AWS Amplify, and connected to the client's data layer, so it can evolve without touching the marketing site.

sections.heading: result
sections.body: A tracking system shaped around their actual workflow, replacing disconnected spreadsheets and email chains.

projects.title: WLAF Ad Platform
projects.tagline: Ad rotator and self-serve management dashboard for a radio station.
projects.summary: A custom WordPress plugin that serves a rotating advertisement slot on a radio station's news site, paired with a Lambda-backed dashboard so station staff can manage advertisers, creatives, and rotation without a developer.

sections.heading: the ask
sections.body: The station sells ad slots on its news site, but every change to an advertiser's image, link, or rotation order came back to a developer. They wanted the revenue side of the site under their own control.

sections.heading: plugin plus dashboard
sections.body: A custom WordPress plugin renders the rotating slot and routes each click through to the advertiser's destination. Creatives live in S3 and are delivered through CloudFront, so the ads never touch the WordPress media library or the site's own bandwidth.

sections.heading: handed over
sections.body: The admin dashboard runs on Lambda and S3, separate from WordPress, so staff can add advertisers and update images, links, and rotation themselves. Changes appear on the live site immediately, with no developer in the loop.

projects.title: Server Checker
projects.tagline: Uptime & health monitoring tool for a 500-site fleet.
projects.summary: An internal server and uptime monitoring tool built to watch over 500+ client sites, alerting on downtime, SSL expiry, and server errors without relying on expensive third-party services.

sections.heading: why build it
sections.body: With 500+ sites under management, manual uptime checking was impossible. Third-party monitoring tools charge per-site, which isn't viable at this scale.

sections.heading: the checker
sections.body: A lightweight service pings every site on a schedule and checks SSL validity, response codes, and server health, then alerts by email or webhook on failure.

sections.heading: where it stands
sections.body: Full visibility over the fleet at near-zero running cost. Average detection time went from hours (a client usually noticing first) to minutes.
